diagnostic:
D5 CORRECTION, S2 rework. The live-replica gate window is now the constant 40 s and the gate reads no reload setting at all, exactly as ADR-IIS-SKR-003, D5 and L12/L13 fix it. The same change serves S3; it was made once and is recorded on both slices.

Production change, five files, all Modified, nothing created or deleted.
crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/reload.rs: BEAT_EVERY becomes pub(crate) where it is, with the reason on it. It does not move, its value stays 10 s and no beat behaviour or row shape changes.
crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/worker.rs: REPLICA_STATE_RETENTION becomes pub(crate) where it is, for the L13 bound. The sweep and its cutoff are untouched.
crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/secrets_key_rotation.rs: LiveOpeners loses its per-instance window field and its INTERVALS = 3, and gains two constants of its own - RELOAD_ENVELOPE = 20 s (the K4 envelope) and WINDOW = 2 * BEAT_EVERY + RELOAD_ENVELOPE, the cadence read where reload.rs owns it, so no second module states 10 s. LiveOpeners::at(now) takes the clock alone, so no call site can widen or narrow the window; opens() compares against Self::WINDOW. The type doc now states the envelope sizing, the mixed-settings counterexample the refused window answers wrongly, and the K6/Y11/I-28a bound above the envelope.
crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs: gate_of(state) drops its Integrations argument and the settings().reload read with it; its doc says the window is the gate's own constant. Three call sites updated.
crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/secrets_key.rs: four gate_of call sites updated, including the closure the POST hands start_over_secrets_key, so the window the apply re-reads inside its locked transaction is the same constant.

Architectural checks at the declared locator, crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/secrets_key_rotation.rs.
T3 (and S3's T5), the generated half of L12: the_gate_counts_a_beat_by_the_window_alone, 256 cases, over the writing server's setting 1 ms to 20 s, the reading server's setting 1 ms to one hour and u64::MAX ms, beat ages from one beat ahead of the reading clock (-10 s) to three times the window (120 s), and opens_secrets_key both true and false, generated together. Each case asserts the gate counts the row exactly while the row says it opens the key and the beat is at most the law's 40 s old, where that 40 s is written in the test as LAW_WINDOW and never read from LiveOpeners; asserts that 40 s is what 2 x BEAT_EVERY plus the envelope comes to; and, for every writer inside the envelope, recomputes the longest gap that server can leave from the rule of reload.rs itself - BEAT_EVERY rounded up to a whole number of its own reload intervals, plus one beat interval of lateness - then asserts that gap plus one whole beat interval still fits the window and that every age inside it reads live. The reading server's setting is carried through each case only to say the answer does not move with it; structurally it has no way in, because at() takes the clock. the_triples_l12_names_read_the_window_alone pins the must-include triples at both truth values of the row: the 5000 ms server read 24 s after its beat by a 200 ms reader, a 1 s beat, the 20 s writer at 39 s and at 41 s, equal settings, a reader slower than the writer, a beat ahead of the clock, and the 1 ms writer with a one-hour reader at 39.999 s; it then spells the refused m9 reading out, that two beat intervals plus the reader's own 200 ms is under 24 s.
T4 (and S3's T6), L13: the_window_never_outlives_the_hour_a_replica_state_row_is_kept crosses the settings at both ends of the admitted range (1 ms, 200 ms, 5000 ms, 20 s, one hour) on either side and asserts at each pair that the window is 2 x BEAT_EVERY plus the envelope, that it is shorter than REPLICA_STATE_RETENTION read in worker.rs, and that the oldest beat the gate still counts on lies inside that retention. Neither constant is restated beside the gate.
the_table_of_the_beats_the_gate_counts_as_a_live_opener, which pinned the old 600 ms window, now reads the 40 s one; its structure, its ahead-of-clock row and its mixed-rows case are unchanged, with the two one-minute ages moved to two minutes so they stay past the window.

Each new check was probed by re-injecting the violation: with WINDOW mutated to lose the reload envelope (2 x BEAT_EVERY alone), cargo test -p foundry-app --lib integrations::secrets_key_rotation exits 101 with four failures - the proptest shrinking to writer 1 ms, reader 1 ms, age 20.001 s, opens true, plus the triples table, the L13 table and the shipped table. The mutant was applied to the VM copy only and the file restored before check-arch ran; the Mac tree never held it.

Commands and observed results, every one in the shared Lima VM through scripts/test-in-lima.sh, each in one foreground invocation wrapped in timeout -k 30 590. cargo fmt then cargo test -p foundry-app --lib integrations::secrets_key_rotation: exit 0, 7 passed, 0 failed, 207 filtered out. cargo test -p foundry-app --lib integrations::handlers: exit 0, 20 passed, 0 failed. The mutant probe: exit 101, 3 passed, 4 failed, as above. cargo xtask check-arch: exit 0, boundary guard PASSED. The us-iis-07 lane through eip_warm and eip_lane: exit 0, 1 feature, 32 scenarios all passed, 571 steps all passed - so S2 run D at instance-integration-setup.feature:1259 and the S3 fifth run at :1532, the two RED at f36b357, now pass, and the other 30 scenarios keep passing. cargo xtask smoke on the final Mac bytes: exit 0, "xtask smoke :: all gates green" over fmt --check, clippy, check-arch and the release workspace tests, 94 test binaries, 1259 tests passed, none failed. A first smoke attempt was cut off by the 590 s bound before its last step finished and its status was never observed; the recorded run is the second, as the root context allows. The unit commands ran as three steps inside one VM invocation; their exit statuses are the inner ones reported above. Nothing was committed and nothing pushed.

Design followed as projected; no contradiction found. No file under crates/foundry-acceptance/, no oracle, support, acceptance, architecture, handoff or ADR file was touched, and no test was weakened, skipped or rewritten. No unit test was added beyond the two declared architectural checks and the corrected shipped table.

Refactors: none. No L1-L4 smell was removed and no responsibility moved, so there is no separate refactor commit.

One deviation from the declared generator note, stated rather than hidden: the proptest runs 256 cases with proptest's default per-run seed and its default source-parallel failure persistence, which is this repository's convention for every other 256-case property and is the file the mutant run actually wrote, crates/foundry-app/proptest-regressions/integrations/secrets_key_rotation.txt. A pinned seed is not set, so "fixed seed" holds only in the sense that a refuting case is persisted beside the module; the law's coverage does not depend on a pinned seed, and no regression file is needed while the property is green.

typesafe: unavailable. jev_decide.py exits 3 with TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from this machine's environment, including a login shell, so no judgment was bought. Two choices stayed open and were settled locally: the window as an associated constant rather than a per-instance field, chosen so a per-instance window cannot be built at all, and the property asserting exact equality against an independently written 40 s plus the independently recomputed longest-gap margin, rather than against the window the type holds.

Local results replace neither the delivery's recorded verification, nor independent review, nor EXAMINE.
